mel.name: Melanoma
mel.description: A malignant tumor of melanocytes. The most dangerous form of skin cancer, capable of spreading to other organs if not detected early.
mel.urgency_message: Immediate dermatologist consultation is strongly recommended. Do not delay.

bcc.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
bcc.description: The most common form of skin cancer. Arises from basal cells in the deepest layer of the epidermis. Rarely metastasizes but can be locally destructive if untreated.
bcc.urgency_message: Schedule a dermatologist appointment as soon as possible for evaluation and treatment.

akiec.name: Actinic Keratoses
akiec.description: A rough, scaly patch caused by years of sun exposure. Considered a precancerous lesion with potential to progress to squamous cell carcinoma.
akiec.urgency_message: Consult a dermatologist. Early treatment prevents progression to invasive carcinoma.

bkl.name: Benign Keratosis
bkl.description: A non-cancerous skin growth including seborrheic keratoses, solar lentigines, and lichen planus-like keratoses. Generally harmless but should be monitored.
bkl.urgency_message: Likely benign, but a routine dermatology check is recommended to confirm.

df.name: Dermatofibroma
df.description: A common benign fibrous nodule usually found on the legs. Caused by a minor injury or insect bite. Very rarely associated with malignancy.
df.urgency_message: Generally benign. Consult a dermatologist if the lesion changes in size, color, or shape.

nv.name: Melanocytic Nevi
nv.description: Commonly known as moles. Benign proliferations of melanocytes. Most are harmless, but atypical nevi may carry a slightly elevated risk of melanoma.
nv.urgency_message: Monitor regularly for changes. Consult a dermatologist if any change in size, border, or color is observed.

vasc.name: Vascular Lesion
vasc.description: Includes cherry angiomas, angiokeratomas, and pyogenic granulomas. Arises from blood vessels in the skin. Typically benign.
vasc.urgency_message: Usually benign. A dermatologist visit is recommended to rule out rare vascular malignancies.
